title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the third draft of 'Analysis situs' (June 1986). On p.108 Grothendieck compares two generalisations of topology without the divisibility axiom. He prefers the one carrying an intrinsic notion of disjointness |·|, which expresses a geometric intuition missing from the purely 'Σ-ensemble' viewpoint. He dismisses his earlier axioms AC(Σ...), AC, AD as artificial, and the page opens with the self-deprecating 'but, un con une fois!'.

He then defines a 'magasin (de multistructures)'. It is a set M with three relations:
- X ≤ Y: X is a piece or stratum of the multistructure Y. Write Ỹ for the set of Y' ≤ Y. Next page: 'Ex: les X̃' are the basic 'figures', i.e. ≤-closed parts.
- X ≪ Y: X lies in the 'ombre' (shadow, closure) of Y. Write Omb(Y) = {Z : Z ≪ Y}.
- X |∘| Y: 'X and Y are strictly/stratifiedly disjoint'. It is later to be written X° ∥ Y° once the 'open parts' X° have a meaning.

Draft axioms (all struck out on this page, rewritten cleanly on p.110):
- Mag1: ≤ and ≪ are orders, and ≤ ⊂ ≪.
- Mag2: for Z ≪ X there is X' ≤ X with Z ≪° X'. Here Z ≪° Y means Y is minimal in Ỹ^{Z} = {Y' ∈ Ỹ : Z ≪ Y'}. A marginal note weakens this to the mere existence of a minimal element; p.110 strengthens it to a least element.
- Mag3: if Y ≪ X, X' ≤ X and Z ≪ Y and Z ≪ X', then there is Y' ≤ Y with Z ≪ Y' ≪ X'. Equivalently, Omb(Y) ∩ Omb(X') = Omb(Y_{X'}) with Y_{X'} = Ỹ ∩ Omb(X'). This says the shadow of a piece meets the shadow of a stratum along shadows of sub-pieces, a frontier-type condition. One may assume Y ≤ X ⇒ Y ≤ X'.
- Margin variant: if Z ≪° Y and Z ≪ X' then Y ≪ X'. That is, Z behaves like a relative generic point of Y: anything whose shadow contains Z contains Y. This is the specialisation and genericity behaviour of strata in a stratified space or scheme.

On p.110 the third relation gets its own axioms. |∘| is symmetric, irreflexive and stable under passing to ≪°-generic sub-pieces. Distinct strata of the same X are disjoint. From this he derives the notions ⊼ and ∥ and 'figures'.

Purpose: to axiomatise abstractly the combinatorics of stratified 'multistructures' (strata, closure/adherence, disjointness), in the spirit of the tame-topology programme of the Esquisse. The ordered set of strata and their incidences is taken as a primitive structure, rather than starting from a topological space.
errors: Mag2 as first written says 'Z est élément minimal de Ỹ^{≥Z}', but Z is not in general an element of Ỹ. It must be Y that is minimal. The margin and the rewrite on p.110 ('a un plus petit élément. Si c'est X, on écrit Z ≪° X') correct this.
Ỹ is used without definition on this page. From p.110 it is evidently {Y' ≤ Y}.

Combined with p.110 Mag4 (distinct Y,Z ≤ X are disjoint) and the irreflexivity of |∘|, taking Y = X gives X disjoint from its own strata. That clashes with the intended intuition unless ≤ is read so that X̃ is a partition of X with X itself as a degenerate case. The axiom system is not yet coherent at this stage.
Mag3 is garbled in the draft: the hypotheses are written in a stacked layout and then struck out. It is replaced on p.110 by an axiom of a different nature, about disjointness.

ideas.what: Abstract 'magasin': a set of pieces with a part/stratum order ≤, a closure/shadow order ≪ containing ≤, and a disjointness relation |∘|
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic poset of strata / abstract stratified set; close in spirit to mereotopology (part-of, connection/contact, disjointness)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Abstract stratified sets: Whitney, Thom, Mather. Contact algebras / mereotopology: Whitehead, de Laguna, Clarke, Düntsch–Vakarelov
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of tame topology / stratified structures in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6; this axiomatisation is not there

ideas.what: Omb(X), the 'shadow' of X, and the generic-incidence relation Z ≪° Y (Y minimal among strata of a piece whose shadow contains Z)
ideas.modern_name: Closure of a stratum / specialisation order; generic point of an irreducible closed set
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (scheme theory, Alexandrov topology of stratifications)

ideas.what: Mag3: the shadow of a piece intersected with the shadow of a stratum equals the shadow of a sub-piece
'Opacité' variant: if Z is generic in Y and Z ≪ X' then Y ≪ X'
ideas.modern_name: Relative generic point / constructibility of closure along strata

missed.claim: Grothendieck takes as primitive a 'part' order together with an intrinsic disjointness relation, which he insists is not reducible to the set-theoretic viewpoint. This matches the region-based, point-free approach of mereotopology and contact algebras. The tame-topology / stratification literature has not drawn this link.
missed.quote: La relation X|∘|Y se lit "X et Y [strictement?] disjoints", on pourra aussi plus loin l'écrire X°∥Y°
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Suggests a point-free, mereotopological axiomatisation of tame/o-minimal stratified geometry, which is a modest but unexplored bridge.

missed.claim: The 'magasin' axiomatics of multistructures is abandoned in draft form. Mag4 is left empty here and the system is inconsistent with the intended reading, as noted under errors. No published follow-up exists.
missed.quote: Un magazin (de multistructures) est la donnée d'un ensemble M, muni de trois relations ≤, ≪, |∘|
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only as a historical document of Grothendieck's attempts at a foundations-level 'analysis situs' for tame topology.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a struck-out draft definition, rewritten on the next page. The ingredients (strata, closure order, frontier condition, generic points) are standard, and the novelty lies only in the unusual packaging with an intrinsic disjointness relation. It is of mild interest for the history of his tame-topology project.
transcription_corrections: First line likely 'but, un con une fois!' (continuing the self-deprecating sentence from p.108); fine as transcribed.
'stratifiquement disjoints' is uncertain; the handwriting may read 'strictement disjoints'.
In Mag2 the struck symbol is '∃' replaced by '∀ Z∈M avec Z≪X'; the definition set is written Ỹ^{Z} (with a superscript Z) rather than Ỹ^{≥Z}.
Left margin by Mag2: 'i.e. ∃ élément minimal dans Ỹ^Z'.
Bottom-left margin 'Variante (Opacité?) ... i.e. Z est un point ... relatif ...': the final words are likely 'point générique relatif' rather than 'point relatif éliminant'; uncertain.
